## User story As a maintainer, I want a workflow that builds and tests every pull request, so that a PR's verdict comes from somewhere other than whichever machine happened to run `swift test` last. ## Acceptance criteria 1. A workflow runs on `pull_request` targeting `main` and on `push` to `main`. 2. It runs the profile's *Build & test* commands: `swift build` then `swift test`, from `ElliotKit`. 3. Its `pull_request` trigger has **no branch filter that excludes `main`** — the portfolio's single most common CI defect is `branches: [main]` on a repo whose default is something else. 4. A failing test fails the job, and the failure is readable from the run log without a local checkout. 5. The run completes in a bounded time — the suite is deterministic since #18, so a job that hangs is a regression, not a flake. A job-level `timeout-minutes` makes that visible. ## Problem There is no `.github/workflows/` in this repository, and branch protection is off (`required_status_checks.enforcement_level: "off"`). Nothing runs when a pull request opens. This is not theoretical. **#18, #19 and #20 — roughly 6 000 added lines — were merged to `main` on the strength of `swift test` run locally on one machine.** That verdict was real, but it is not shared: nobody else can reproduce it, nothing recorded it, and the next contributor has no signal at all. `merge-pr` has an entire step for waiting on CI that this repo turns into a no-op. It also means the two guarantees this codebase works hardest for are unenforced. #18 made the suite terminate reliably; nothing stops the next change from making it hang again. #20 made `ElliotMCPKit` testable; nothing stops those tests from rotting. ## Proposed solution One workflow, `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, on a macOS runner (the package is `platforms: [.macOS(.v15)]` and the app is SwiftUI, so Linux is not an option). Build, then test. Nothing else yet — no lint gate until issue for `.swift-format` is settled, no app-bundle step, no matrix. Deliberately minimal: the value is having *a* shared verdict, and every gate added before the first one is green is a gate that delays it. Once it is green on `main`, turn on branch protection requiring the check, so the gate is real rather than advisory. ## Area `none` — repository tooling. No SwiftPM target changes.
🧠 Brainstorm **Problem/context.** `.claude/skills/repo-profile.md` records the gap explicitly, in two places: the *CI gates* section says "there is no `.github/workflows/` in this repo — nothing runs on a PR", and "Until a workflow exists, 'green CI' is not a thing merge-pr can wait for." PR #19's own follow-up section raised it independently. The repo already has a documented, cheap, deterministic test command (`cd ElliotKit && swift test`, ~0.5 s, no tokens, no GitHub access — it drives `Scripts/fake-claude.sh`). Everything needed to run CI already exists; only the workflow is missing. **Approaches.** 1. *Minimal macOS build+test workflow.* One job, two steps. Cheap to write, cheap to review, and it turns the existing local verdict into a shared one. Downside: macOS runners are the expensive kind of GitHub minutes, and this is a private repository, so runs draw on quota. 2. *Add lint/format to the same workflow.* Tempting, but the formatting question is unsettled — `swift format lint --strict` currently reports 8242 errors on untouched `main`. Landing this together means the first CI run is red for a reason unrelated to correctness, which is the fastest way to teach everyone to ignore the badge. 3. *Self-hosted runner.* Solves the macOS-minutes cost, and the portfolio already has a note that a self-hosted runner would be free and unlimited for the org's private repos. But it is infrastructure to own before there is any CI at all. **Recommendation.** Approach 1. Get one honest green check first; treat cost (3) and lint (2) as separate decisions once there is something to measure. The suite is 0.5 s of compute — the runner minutes are dominated by checkout and toolchain setup, not by us.
📋 Spec **Goal.** Every PR to `main` carries a build+test verdict that is not a claim about someone's laptop. **Non-goals.** Formatting/lint enforcement; building `dist/Elliot.app`; a Swift-version matrix; code coverage; notarisation. **Shape.** ```yaml name: CI on: pull_request: branches: [main] push: branches: [main] ``` `branches: [main]` is correct **here** because `main` genuinely is this repo's default branch (profile, *Identity*). Recording that explicitly matters: the same two lines are a latent bug in any repo whose default is `dev`, which is the majority of the surrounding portfolio. One job, `build-and-test`, on `macos-15` (or the newest image carrying a Swift 6.1 toolchain — the package declares `swift-tools-version: 6.1` and `swiftLanguageModes: [.v6]`). Steps: `actions/checkout` → verify the toolchain (`swift --version`, so a runner-image drift shows up as its own line rather than as a mystery compile error) → `swift build` → `swift test`, all with `working-directory: ElliotKit`. `timeout-minutes` on the job. The suite runs in about half a second and issue #7's whole subject was a hang that presented as a broken toolchain; a bounded job turns a recurrence into a red check instead of a stuck queue. **Edge cases.** - The end-to-end suite spawns `Scripts/fake-claude.sh`; it must stay executable through checkout (git preserves the mode bit — worth one assertion in the first run rather than an assumption). - The suite needs no `gh` auth and no network. If a future test does, it must be marked, not silently granted a token. **Assumptions.** GitHub-hosted macOS runners are acceptable for this private repo's quota. If not, that is issue-worthy on its own and does not block writing the workflow.
## 🛠️ Implementation plan > **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking. **Goal.** A shared build+test verdict on every PR. **Architecture.** No SwiftPM targets change. Only `.github/workflows/ci.yml` is added. **Tech stack.** GitHub Actions, macOS runner, Swift 6.1. **Global constraints.** - Commit identity: `git -c user.email=phmatray@gmail.com -c user.name="Philippe Matray"`. - Build & test, verbatim from the profile: `cd ElliotKit && swift build`, `cd ElliotKit && swift test`. - Do not add a lint/format step — it belongs to the `.swift-format` decision and would land red. - Do not touch `Package.swift` or any source file. ### Task 1: The workflow, building and testing on every PR **Files:** create `.github/workflows/ci.yml`. **Interfaces:** job `build-and-test`; triggers `pull_request: [main]` and `push: [main]`. - [ ] **Step 1:** Write `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — `macos-15`, `actions/checkout@v5`, `swift --version`, `swift build`, `swift test`, `working-directory: ElliotKit`, `timeout-minutes: 20`. - [ ] **Step 2:** Verify locally that the exact commands pass from a clean checkout: `cd ElliotKit && swift build && swift test` → expect 326 tests passing. - [ ] **Step 3:** Commit: `ci: build and test every pull request`. - [ ] **Step 4:** Open the PR and read the first real run. Confirm the job is **not** skipped — a skipped job here means the trigger is wrong, which is the exact defect this issue exists to avoid. - [ ] **Step 5:** Confirm the run's test count matches the local one. A lower number means a suite did not run on the runner. ### Task 2: Prove the gate actually fails **Files:** none permanently — a throwaway commit on the PR branch. **Interfaces:** none. - [ ] **Step 1:** On the PR branch, temporarily break one assertion (e.g. flip an `#expect` in `ProcessRunnerTests`) and push. - [ ] **Step 2:** Confirm the check goes **red**, and that the failing test's name and message are readable in the run log without a local checkout. - [ ] **Step 3:** Revert the deliberate break and push; confirm the check returns green. - [ ] **Step 4:** Commit: `ci: verify the gate fails on a real failure` (or fold into Task 1's commit if the revert leaves no diff). ### Task 3: Make the check required **Files:** none in-repo — GitHub branch-protection settings. **Interfaces:** branch protection on `main`. - [ ] **Step 1:** After the workflow is green on `main`, enable branch protection requiring the `build-and-test` check. - [ ] **Step 2:** Confirm `gh api repos/phmatray/Elliot/branches/main/protection` reports the check as required. - [ ] **Step 3:** Record in `.claude/skills/repo-profile.md` that CI now exists, replacing the two `TODO` notes in *Build & test* and *CI gates* that say it does not. - [ ] **Step 4:** Commit: `docs(profile): CI exists — record the real gate`.

## User story **As a** developer opening a repository in Elliot, **I want** the board to already show that repository's GitHub issues and pull requests in the right columns, with a **Refresh** button to pull in what has changed since, **so that** Elliot is the control room for work that already exists rather than only for work I typed into it after installing Elliot. ## Acceptance criteria 1. The mapping is a **pure function** in `ElliotModel`: no PR → **To Do** · draft PR → **In Progress** · ready PR → **In Review** · merged, or a closed issue → **Done**. **Never Backlog** — backlog means *not filed*, and everything imported is filed by definition. 2. An issue and the pull request that closes it are **one unit**, paired by the existing `PRMatcher`. A pull request no issue claims (a Renovate bump, a direct `refactor(mcp):`) is a unit of its own, and a pull request is claimed by **at most one** issue. 3. `GitHubImporter.plan(repoID:issues:pullRequests:existingCards:dismissed:now:)` returns `create` / `adopt` / `unchanged` actions and is **idempotent**: feeding back the cards its own `create`s describe yields nothing but `unchanged`. 4. **Ownership is first-come and permanent** — a card already carrying issue #11 or PR 20 keeps it, whatever the linkage looks like on this pass — and **the plan advances a card, never rewinds it**: a card in In Progress with a run in flight is not demoted to To Do because this pass saw no PR yet. 5. An **additive `v2` migration** adds two partial unique indexes, `(repoID, issueNumber)` and `(repoID, prNumber)`, plus a `dismissedExternal` table. A `v1` database opens with its cards intact, and a second card claiming the same issue is rejected **by the database**, not merely by the planner. 6. `GHIssue` gains `body`, `GHClient.issues` requests it, and both payloads decode from **captured real fixtures** committed under `Fixtures/gh/` — the same `--json` field sets the client sends, so client and fixture cannot drift apart silently. 7. All of it is proven by `swift test` with no GUI and no writes outside `FileManager.default.temporaryDirectory`. **This issue ships no user-visible change.** It is the decision layer plus the persistence and the two read-only sources it needs. The service that applies a plan, the Refresh button, and dismiss-on-delete are **#17** — the split is deliberate, and the reason is in the brainstorm. ## Problem Open Elliot on the Elliot repository today and the board is **empty**, while `github.com/phmatray/Elliot` has 7 open issues and 6 pull requests. Nothing is broken — it is that a card only ever comes into existence one way, `BoardService.createCard` (`ElliotEngine/BoardService.swift:153`), reached from the *New story* sheet or `board_create_card`; and a card only ever learns an issue number by **having filed it** — `Verifier` reads `gh issue list` after a `create-issue` run and writes the number back (`ElliotEngine/Verifier.swift:46`). So the board's knowledge starts on the day Elliot was installed. Everything before that is invisible to it, and the README's own promise — *"no way to see at a glance what is waiting, what is running, and what is stuck on CI"* — is kept only for work Elliot itself created. What makes the gap conspicuous is that the plumbing is **already here and already exercised**: - `GHClient.issues(repo:limit:)` and `GHClient.pullRequests(repo:limit:)` (`ElliotProcess/GHClient.swift:78,93`) already list a whole repository. Both are called on every verification pass; neither is ever used to *populate* anything. - `PRMatcher` (`ElliotModel/PRMatcher.swift`) already scores a pull request against an issue number by branch, title and closing keyword — the exact pairing an import needs, trailing-hyphen anchor and all. - `PRWatcher` already polls `gh pr list` per repository every 15–60 s and already moves cards to In Review and Done on its own — but only for cards that **already exist** and sit in In Progress or In Review (`ElliotEngine/PRWatcher.swift:56`). And there is **no refresh anywhere in the app**. `AppModel.refreshRepoChecks` is Preflight's, not the board's; the board's only path back to reality is `Reconciler.sweep()` at launch, which re-derives cards it already knows about. The toolbar has *New story* and *Preflight* and nothing else (`ElliotApp/BoardView.swift:35-63`). And **nothing stops two cards claiming the same issue.** Today only the verifier writes `issueNumber`, to exactly one card, so it has never mattered; an import makes it matter on every pass. That is this issue's `v2` migration. (Its sibling — `BoardService.updateCard` guarding on `issueNumber` but not on `prNumber`, so an imported Renovate card would be editable and the edit would go nowhere — only bites once cards can actually be imported, so it is #17's.) ## Proposed solution A **pure planner** in `ElliotModel` — `GitHubImporter.plan(…)` returning `create` / `adopt` / `unchanged` actions — with the persistence that makes those actions safe to apply: an additive `v2` migration where duplicate ownership is impossible, and a `gh` payload rich enough to build a card from. #17 is the thin service that applies a plan through the funnels that already exist. `ElliotApp` is an `executableTarget` with no test target (`Package.swift:23`), so the judgement cannot live in the view. The argument #5 made for `CardDraft` and #11 makes for the reconciler applies here, and more sharply: this decides *which column a card lands in*, and getting that wrong in In Review means firing `merge-pr` at a pull request nobody asked to merge. The view gets a button; the model gets the rules. ## Area `model` (`ElliotModel` — `GitHubImporter`, the testable core) with supporting changes in `store` (the `v2` migration, dismissals) and `process` (`GHIssue.body` and the captured fixtures). **Related:** #11, #12, #13 — the repository-fleet family. They answer *which repositories exist*; this answers *what is in flight inside one*. Independent of all three: nothing here needs the tree layout or the reconciler, and nothing there needs this.
🧠 Brainstorm ### What constrains the design **The board is a remote control, not a mirror.** The README's first line is that *"moving a card is the act of execution"*. Anything imported therefore has to be a **real card** — draggable, and dragging it must do the real thing. That is also the prize: with this, opening Elliot on Elliot and dragging the #11 card from To Do to In Progress runs `implement-issue 11` against the actual issue. **A column is a claim about reality, and In Review is armed.** In Review → Done runs `merge-pr`. The placement rule is not cosmetic, and it belongs where `swift test` can reach it — which `ElliotApp`, having no test target (`Package.swift:42-49`), is not. **Idempotence is the whole feature.** A refresh button that duplicates cards is worse than no refresh button, because the duplicates are indistinguishable from real work. ### The open question: what an imported issue *is* to the board **A. Import as ordinary cards, adopt on every refresh.** *(recommended)* - ✅ Imported cards are cards: draggable, and the drag does the real thing. - ✅ Reuses every funnel — `BoardService` for the column, `PRMatcher` for pairing — and `PRWatcher` picks the new cards up for free, since it watches by column, not by provenance. - ✅ The hard part is a pure function of four lists, so the whole matrix is testable without a database. - ⚠️ Needs dedup that cannot drift, and a tombstone so "I deleted that card" survives a refresh. Both are small, and both are in the plan. **B. A read-only GitHub overlay — ghost items rendered beside the cards.** - ✅ No migration, no dedup, no tombstones; the store stays exactly as it is. - ❌ Ghosts cannot be dragged, so the board would show work it refuses to act on — the precise opposite of the README's thesis. - ❌ Two kinds of thing in one column is a UI lie: the count in the column header would mean two different things depending on what it counted. - ❌ You would immediately want to "promote" a ghost to a card, which is option A with an extra state. **C. Extend `PRWatcher` to create cards as well as reconcile them.** - ✅ Cheapest — the poll loop already lists pull requests per repository. - ❌ It is an actor on a 15–300 s backoff timer. Making a background poller a *creator* means a bug invents cards on a loop, unattended, with no user gesture to blame it on. - ❌ Still no refresh button, which is half of what was asked for. - ❌ It watches only In Progress / In Review cards; teaching it to see everything changes its cost model from "cards in flight" to "the whole repository", every 15 s. ### Recommendation **A.** B and C both start from "avoid the migration", and the migration is the cheap part. What actually has to be got right is *never create the same card twice* and *never fire a skill by importing* — and only A puts both under `swift test`. ### Why this is two issues and not one The whole feature is a seven-task plan across five targets, and its plan does not fit in one GitHub issue body (65 536 characters). That constraint only exposed a seam that was already there, and that this repository has already used once: **#11 decides, #12 acts.** Same shape here — - **this issue** *decides and persists*: the pure planner, the migration, the payloads. Nothing on screen changes, and every rule it establishes is provable by `swift test`; - **#17** *applies and shows*: `GitHubImportService`, dismiss-on-delete, the Refresh button. The seam is real rather than administrative: the follow-up consumes this issue's `plan()` and touches no model rule, and this issue's tests need nothing the follow-up builds. ### The two rules that kill the edge cases **Ownership is first-come and permanent.** If a card already carries PR 14, that pull request is that card's, whatever this pass thinks about linkage. Without it: refresh 1 creates a standalone card for PR #14 (it closes nothing); someone later edits the body to say `Closes #11`; refresh 2 wants to attach PR 14 to the #11 card while the standalone still holds it — two cards, one PR, and a unique-index violation on write. With it, that whole class disappears and the rule is one line to test. **Import advances, never rewinds.** The computed column is applied only when it is strictly later in board order. A card in In Progress with `implement-issue` running has no pull request yet; a naïve recompute would drag it back to To Do mid-run. Demotion belongs to the components holding real evidence — `PRWatcher` records *"The pull request was closed without being merged."* and leaves the column alone (`PRWatcher.swift:115`); import copies that restraint. ### Rejected: filtering bots `gh` exposes `author.is_bot`, so dropping the Renovate dashboard issue and the Renovate pull requests would be a *fact*, not a guess. Rejected anyway: a Renovate PR sitting in In Review that you drag to Done genuinely runs `merge-pr` on it, which is the app working as advertised. The Dependency Dashboard issue is the only real noise, and dismissal handles it in one gesture — without hardcoding a policy about whose work counts. ### Assumptions Stated rather than asked, per this skill's autonomy contract: - **Open items only.** Closed issues and merged pull requests no card knows about are history, not work; importing them would make Done a graveyard on first run. Items an existing card already tracks are still reconciled whatever their state. One line in the service if it should change. - **Import on selection, not at launch.** One repository's import is two `gh` calls; every enabled repository at every launch is 2×N, the wrong shape once #12 lands and N is 221. The button covers the rest. - **`story` stays `nil`.** An imported issue is not a user story, and parsing role/want/benefit back out of arbitrary prose would be inventing. The issue body goes in `body`, which `Card.displayTitle` and the detail sheet already handle. - **`createdAt` is the GitHub object's, `columnEnteredAt` is now.** The work is as old as the issue; the card only just arrived in its column, and claiming otherwise would falsify the one timestamp the board uses to say how long something has been sitting.
📋 Spec ### Goal One gesture — selecting a repository, or pressing Refresh — makes the board show what GitHub already knows about that repository, without starting anything and without ever creating the same card twice. ### Non-goals - Writing to GitHub. Import is strictly read-only (`gh issue list`, `gh pr list`). - Replacing `PRWatcher`. It keeps doing continuous reconciliation of in-flight cards; import is the cold start and the on-demand catch-up. - Importing labels, assignees, milestones or comments — `Card` has nowhere to put them. - Syncing card edits *back* to an issue. Editing stays refused, which is #5's rule extended. ### The mapping ```mermaid flowchart TD I["gh issue list --state all
number, title, body, url, state, createdAt"] --> G P["gh pr list --state all
number, title, body, headRefName, isDraft, state, mergedAt"] --> G G["group
PRMatcher.bestMatch pairs a PR with its issue
an unclaimed PR is a unit of its own"] --> U{{"unit = issue? + pullRequest?"}} U --> Q1{"PR merged
or issue closed?"} Q1 -->|yes| DONE["Done"] Q1 -->|no| Q2{"has an open PR?"} Q2 -->|no| TODO["To Do"] Q2 -->|"yes — draft"| PROG["In Progress"] Q2 -->|"yes — ready"| REV["In Review"] BL["Backlog — unreachable"]:::ghost classDef ghost fill:#eee,stroke:#999,stroke-dasharray:4,color:#777 ``` Backlog is unreachable by construction: it is the column for a story that has not been filed, and everything on this diagram has a number. A closed-unmerged pull request whose issue is **still open** maps to **To Do** — the branch was abandoned, the work was not. ### Types All new, in `ElliotModel/GitHubImport.swift` — pure: no I/O, no clock, no randomness (`now` is a parameter), exactly as `evaluateMove` is. Full definitions are in Tasks 1 and 2. | Type | What it is | |---|---| | `ExternalKind` · `ExternalRef` | `(issue\|pullRequest, number)` — the dedup key *and* the dismissal key | | `ImportUnit` | one issue, its pull request, or both — what becomes one card | | `CardSeed` | a card that does not exist yet. **No `orderIndex`**: only the store can allocate one | | `AdoptedFields` | the fields an adoption overwrites, and only those | | `ImportAction` | `.create(CardSeed)` · `.adopt(cardID:fields:moveTo:)` · `.unchanged(cardID:)` | | `ImportPlan` | the actions plus `skippedDismissed`, and `created`/`adopted`/`moved`/`unchanged` counts | ```swift public enum GitHubImporter { public static func group(issues: [GHIssue], pullRequests: [GHPullRequest]) -> [ImportUnit] public static func column(for unit: ImportUnit) -> Column public static func plan( repoID: UUID, issues: [GHIssue], pullRequests: [GHPullRequest], existingCards: [Card], dismissed: Set, now: Date ) -> ImportPlan } ``` `GHIssue` gains `body: String?` and `isClosed`. `MoveOrigin.SystemReason` gains `githubImport`. `allowsSideEffects` already returns `false` for every `.system` case and `evaluateMove` already short-circuits to `.noAction` on it (`RuleEngine.swift:101`) — so criterion 5 is satisfied by the existing rule engine, and the test asserts it rather than new code implementing it. ### Persistence — migration `v2_github_import` (additive) ```sql CREATE UNIQUE INDEX card_on_repo_issue ON card(repoID, issueNumber) WHERE issueNumber IS NOT NULL; CREATE UNIQUE INDEX card_on_repo_pr ON card(repoID, prNumber) WHERE prNumber IS NOT NULL; CREATE TABLE dismissedExternal ( repoID TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES repo(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, kind TEXT NOT NULL, number INTEGER NOT NULL, dismissedAt DATETIME NOT NULL, PRIMARY KEY (repoID, kind, number) ); ``` A `v1` database survives untouched: no column dropped, no row rewritten. The indexes cannot fail to build on existing data — `issueNumber` and `prNumber` are written today only by `Verifier`/`PRWatcher`, onto exactly one card each. ### Flow ``` AppModel.refreshFromGitHub() └─ GitHubImportService.importRepo(repo) [ElliotEngine, actor] ├─ gh.issues(repo:) · gh.pullRequests(repo:) read-only ├─ store.cards(repoID:) · store.dismissals(repoID:) ├─ GitHubImporter.plan(…) pure └─ apply: .create(seed) → board.adoptCard(seed) allocates orderIndex, one write .adopt(id,f,move?) → store.saveCard(…) board.applySystemMove(…, .githubImport) ← never fires a skill .unchanged → nothing ``` `BoardService.adoptCard(_:)` is a new method rather than an argument on `createCard`: adoption sets an issue number and a column in the same write, and folding that into the path the *user's* New-story sheet takes would make one signature answer to two very different callers. It is still `BoardService`, so "the only thing that changes a card's column" holds. ### Error handling - A `gh` failure for one repository yields `ImportSummary(failure:)` for that repository and does not abort the pass — the same posture #12 requires of its fixes. - A unique-index violation on write is a **planner bug**, not a user condition: surfaced in the summary as a failure rather than swallowed, because silently skipping it would hide the duplicate the index exists to catch. - No network is a plain failure carrying the `gh` message. Import never falls back to stale data, and the status bar says what it could not reach. ### UI `BoardView` toolbar, between *New story* and *Preflight*: a `Menu` whose primary action refreshes and whose one item is **Forget dismissed items**, ⌘R, disabled while importing. The status bar's existing `ProgressView` row is reused, and `status` receives `"Elliot — 6 new · 1 updated · 0 unchanged"`. Auto-import runs once per repository per session from `.task(id: model.selectedRepoID)`, guarded by an in-memory `Set`. Not persisted: a relaunch re-importing is two `gh` calls and is idempotent by criterion 4. ### Testing | Suite | Proves | |---|---| | `ElliotModelTests/GitHubImporterTests` | the whole mapping matrix, pairing via `PRMatcher`, never-Backlog, permanent ownership, forward-only moves, dismissal skipping, and **idempotence** | | `ElliotStoreTests` | `v2` is additive over a populated `v1`; a second card claiming the same `issueNumber` is rejected by the database; dismissals round-trip and cascade | | `ElliotProcessTests` | `GHIssue`/`GHPullRequest` decode **captured real payloads** from `Fixtures/gh/` | `ElliotEngineTests` — proving that applying a plan starts **zero** runs — belongs to **#17**, which is where anything is applied at all.
## 🛠️ Implementation plan > **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking. **Goal:** Decide, and be able to persist, what a repository's GitHub issues and pull requests mean for the board — without applying any of it yet. **Architecture:** A pure planner in `ElliotModel` decides everything (pairing, column, create-vs-adopt); an additive `v2` migration makes duplicate ownership impossible and remembers dismissals; `GHClient` learns to ask for issue bodies. Layers are touched in dependency order — Model → Store → Process. The applier and the button are the follow-up issue. **Tech Stack:** Swift 6.1, `swiftLanguageModes: [.v6]`, SwiftPM, GRDB 7, swift-testing (`@Suite`/`@Test`/`#expect`), SwiftUI, `gh` via `GHClient`. ### Global Constraints - Build and test from `ElliotKit/`: `swift build`, `swift test`, one suite via `swift test --filter `. - Commit identity: `git -c user.email=phmatray@gmail.com -c user.name="Philippe Matray"`. - Commit subjects: `(): `, scope ∈ `model` · `store` · `process` · `engine` · `app`. - Strict Swift 6 concurrency: every new type is `Sendable`; new model value types are `Codable, Sendable, Hashable` like their neighbours. Public structs need an explicit `public init`. - `ElliotModel` has no dependencies and no clock: `plan` takes `now: Date` as a parameter. - `ElliotMCPKit` must keep importing neither `ElliotEngine` nor `ElliotProcess` (`Package.swift:35`). - `BoardService` remains the only thing that changes a card's column. - Nothing in this issue writes to GitHub. - Migrations are additive and append-only; never edit `v1_initial`, never reorder a persisted raw value. --- ### Task 1: Pair issues with pull requests, and map a pair to a column **Files:** create `ElliotKit/Sources/ElliotModel/GitHubImport.swift` · modify `ElliotKit/Sources/ElliotModel/GHPayloads.swift` · test `ElliotKit/Tests/ElliotModelTests/GitHubImporterTests.swift` **Interfaces:** - Consumes: `PRMatcher.bestMatch(among:issue:runStartedAt:)`, `Column`, `GHIssue`, `GHPullRequest`. - Produces: `ExternalKind`, `ExternalRef`, `ImportUnit`, `GitHubImporter.group(issues:pullRequests:) -> [ImportUnit]`, `GitHubImporter.column(for:) -> Column`, `GHIssue.body: String?`, `GHIssue.isClosed: Bool`. - [x] **Step 1: Write the failing test** — create `ElliotKit/Tests/ElliotModelTests/GitHubImporterTests.swift`: ```swift import Foundation import Testing @testable import ElliotModel func issue(_ n: Int, title: String = "Some work", body: String? = title: Work out what a repository's GitHub issues and pull requests mean for the board

body:
## User story **As a** developer running a 200-repository portfolio, **I want** Elliot to work out, from one configured tree root, exactly which of my GitHub repositories are missing, misplaced or unknown to it, **so that** the page that shows and repairs them has a single, tested answer to render instead of re-deriving the truth in a SwiftUI view. ## Acceptance criteria 1. The layout `///` is a **pure function** in `ElliotModel`, both ways: `nameWithOwner` + visibility → expected path, and path → owner/visibility/name. 2. A path that is not exactly `///` for a **configured owner** does not parse. `_local-only/`, `_worktrees/`, `customers/` and `repo-audit/` are **out of scope**, never "misplaced" — nothing downstream may ever propose relocating them. 3. `RepoReconciler.rows(github:disk:registered:layout:)` merges the three sources into one row per repository, each carrying **exactly one verdict** — `.ok`, `.notCloned`, `.notRegistered`, `.missing`, `.misplaced(expected:)`, `.outOfScope(…)` — and the fixes legal for it. 4. Forks and archived repositories are listed **with the reason on screen**, and carry no fix. 5. The tree root, the owner list and a repo's visibility are persisted through an **additive** `v2` migration that leaves a `v1` database intact. 6. `GHClient.repos(owner:)` lists an account through `gh repo list --json`, decoding a **captured real payload** committed as a fixture; `RepoTreeScanner` walks the owner folders **one level deep**. 7. All of it is proven by `swift test` with no GUI and no writes to disk outside `FileManager.default.temporaryDirectory`. **This issue ships no user-visible change.** It is the decision layer: everything that works out *what is wrong*, plus the persistence and the two read-only sources it needs. The Repositories page and the four fix buttons are the follow-up, and the `Sync` sweep the one after that. The split is deliberate — see the brainstorm. ## Problem Registering a repository is one folder at a time. `PreflightView.choose()` (`ElliotKit/Sources/ElliotApp/PreflightView.swift:139`) opens an `NSOpenPanel`, and `AppModel.addRepo(path:)` (`ElliotKit/Sources/ElliotApp/AppModel.swift:315`) resolves `nameWithOwner` and `defaultBranch` through `gh repo view` and saves one `Repo`. The README says so itself: *"registering a repository is UI-only (no CLI)"* (`README.md:139`). Fine for the two or three repositories Elliot has been driven against. Measured on this machine: ```console $ for d in ~/Repositories/{phmatray,Atypical-Consulting}/{public,private}; do printf "%4s %s\n" "$(ls -1 "$d" | wc -l | tr -d ' ')" "$d"; done 45 /Users/phmatray/Repositories/phmatray/public 136 /Users/phmatray/Repositories/phmatray/private 25 /Users/phmatray/Repositories/Atypical-Consulting/public 15 /Users/phmatray/Repositories/Atypical-Consulting/private ``` **221 clones**, against a GitHub portfolio the control room's inventory puts at 343 repositories. Adding them by hand is 221 open-panel round trips — and the result would be registered without ever being *checked*, because: - **Nothing knows where a repository should live.** `Repo` (`ElliotKit/Sources/ElliotModel/Repo.swift:7`) holds a `path` and a `nameWithOwner` with no relation between them. A clone under the wrong owner — or under `public/` when the repository is private — is invisible to Elliot by design. - **Nothing asks GitHub what exists.** `GHClient` (`ElliotKit/Sources/ElliotProcess/GHClient.swift:9`) can identify the repository in a directory (`repoInfo(cwd:)`) but cannot list an account, so a repository that was never cloned cannot appear anywhere. Part of the adjacent problem is solved elsewhere and must not be reinvented: `repo-audit/repo_sync.py` classifies every clone under its guarded roots into `FRESH` or `BLOCKED:{dirty,ahead,diverged,detached,no-remote,unreadable,fetch-failed}`, with 62 tests behind it. What it deliberately does **not** do is talk to GitHub: it reconciles disk against `origin`, never disk against the *account*, so it cannot report a repository that exists and was never cloned, or one filed under the wrong owner. That account-side gap is what this issue computes. ## Proposed solution A **pure function of three lists** — GitHub, disk, store — returning one row per repository with a single verdict and the fixes legal for it, living in `ElliotModel`, which has no dependencies and is where `swift test` can reach it. `ElliotApp` is an `executableTarget` (`ElliotKit/Package.swift:23`) with no test target — the argument #5 made for `CardDraft` applies here and more sharply: the verdict *misplaced* will be acted on by **moving a directory in Philippe's portfolio**, so it has to be provable rather than eyeballed. Around it: an additive `v2` migration for the layout setting and a repo's visibility, `gh repo list` per owner, and a deliberately shallow tree scan. ## Area `model` (`ElliotModel` — the layout and the reconciler, the testable core), with supporting changes in `store` (the `v2` migration), `process` (`GHClient.repos(owner:)`) and `engine` (the scanner).
🧠 Brainstorm ### What constrains the design **`ElliotApp` cannot be tested.** `Package.swift:23` declares it an `executableTarget`; the test targets (`Package.swift:42-49`) cover Model, Store, Process, Engine and IPC — not App. Any rule living in a SwiftUI view is unprovable by `swift test`. #5 already paid this and pushed the answer down into `CardDraft`; the same move is mandatory here, because the rule being decided will end in `moveItem`. **The tree has more roots than the two accounts.** Alongside `phmatray/` and `Atypical-Consulting/` sit `_local-only/`, `_worktrees/`, `customers/`, `repo-audit/`, `dotnet/` and `NuGetMonorepo/`. A scanner that walks the root assuming `//` classifies every one of them as *misplaced* and offers to move it — including the linked worktrees and the clone carrying the portfolio's own tooling. **`repo.path` is `UNIQUE`** (`Migrations.swift:11`), so importing 221 clones twice is idempotent for free, keyed on the path. ### Approaches **A. A layout value type plus a pure reconciler over three lists.** *(recommended)* `RepoTreeLayout` maps `nameWithOwner` + visibility ⇄ `///`; `RepoReconciler` turns (GitHub, disk, store) into `[RepoRow]`, each with one `RepoIssue` and its legal `RepoFix`es. The page and the fixes consume it later without re-deriving anything. - ✅ The verdict — including *misplaced* — is a pure function in a dependency-free target: a unit test rather than something you check by clicking a button that moves a directory. - ✅ One place decides. The page renders, the service applies; neither judges. - ✅ Leaves room for the sync half without reshaping anything: a probe *refines* a row's verdict, it does not change how rows are built. - ⚠️ Ships no UI on its own. Accepted deliberately — see below. **B. Shell out to `repo-audit/repo_sync.py`.** - ✅ Zero duplicated logic; 62 tests already stand behind it. - ❌ **Answers a different question** — disk vs `origin`. It cannot report a repository that exists on GitHub and was never cloned, or one filed under the wrong owner, which is the whole of this issue. - ❌ Welds a self-contained macOS app to a Python script in a directory that is not a repository Elliot knows, found by a hardcoded path, adding Python 3 as a runtime dependency of the `.app`. - ❌ Its remediation is `pull` and "human arbitration, printed" — no per-row verdict to render. **C. Work it out in the view: scan and compare inside `RepositoriesView`.** - ✅ Fewest types, fastest to a screenshot. - ❌ Puts the "this directory is in the wrong place" judgement in the one target `swift test` cannot reach, immediately before the button that acts on it. - ❌ The sync follow-up would then need the same judgement a second time, in a service — two copies of the rule, which is exactly what `BoardService`'s single-funnel decision exists to prevent. ### Recommendation **A**. B answers *disk vs `origin`* while the question is *disk vs the account*, and it would make a signed macOS app depend on an unversioned script outside every repository it knows. C is how you get two divergent copies of a rule whose failure mode is moving the wrong directory. ### Why this is three issues The work splits at two honest seams, and each side is a reviewable PR: 1. **What is wrong** — this issue. Pure, testable, no writes. 2. **Show it and repair it** — the Repositories page plus `clone` / `move` / `register` / `forget`. The first thing in Elliot that writes outside a `.git` directory it was handed. 3. **Keep it fresh** — `fetch`, ahead/behind, `pull --ff-only`, a `Sync` button. The only part that writes *inside* a working tree, and the only part needing bounded concurrency over 221 repositories. Keeping them together would have produced one issue too large for a single review and, more to the point, one PR mixing a pure value type with `FileManager.moveItem`. This issue's `RepoIssue` therefore carries only the verdicts it can produce; the sync issue adds the git-state cases. ### The decision this issue locks in: what the downstream fixes may do Even though nothing here writes, the enum written here is what the buttons will be allowed to offer, so it is decided now: `clone` creates what did not exist; `move` relocates a directory and must refuse an occupied destination; `register` / `forget` are database writes only, and `forget` never touches the disk. **Nothing deletes** — no clone, no remote, no branch. The portfolio learned this one the expensive way: six clones deleted on the strength of a `git status --porcelain -uno`, precisely the option that hides untracked files. There is no `.delete` case in `RepoFix`, and there must never be one. ### Assumptions Stated rather than asked, per this skill's autonomy contract: the owners are `phmatray` and `Atypical-Consulting`; the visibility folder comes from GitHub's `visibility` field (`PUBLIC` → `public`, everything else — `INTERNAL` included — → `private`); and `gh repo list --limit 1000` covers the portfolio, with archived repositories listed and flagged rather than filtered out, so "why is this not here?" always has an answer.
📋 Spec ### Goal Compute, for every repository of the configured owners, exactly one verdict describing how GitHub, the disk and the store disagree — as a pure function, with the persistence and the two read-only sources it needs. ### Scope `RepoTreeLayout` / `RepoSlot` / `RepoVisibility`; `RepoIssue` / `RepoFix` / `RepoRow` / `RepoReconciler`; an additive `v2` migration for the layout setting and `repo.visibility`; `GHClient.repos(owner:)`; `RepoTreeScanner`. ### Non-goals - **No writes.** No `clone`, `move`, `register`, `forget`, `pull` or `fetch` — the `RepoFix` cases are *declared* here and applied by the follow-up. - No UI. No `AppModel` change, no new view. - No delete, ever — there is no `.delete` case to add later. - No support for the tree's other roots (`_local-only/`, `_worktrees/`, `customers/`, `repo-audit/`): out of scope by construction, never "misplaced". - No change to the board, to `BoardService`, or to how a card moves. Repositories are not cards. - No new MCP tool. The helper stays read-only and unchanged. ### Data flow ```mermaid flowchart TD GH["GHClient.repos(owner:)
gh repo list --json"] DISK["RepoTreeScanner.scan()
owner / visibility / name"] REG["BoardStore.repos()
already registered"] GH --> REC DISK --> REC REG --> REC REC["RepoReconciler.rows(...)
pure — ElliotModel"] REC --> ROWS["[RepoRow]
one issue + legal fixes"] ROWS -.-> NEXT["the page and the fixes
follow-up issue"] ``` ### Verdicts and the fix each will carry | `RepoIssue` | Meaning | Fix declared | |---|---|---| | `.ok` | registered, present, right folder | — | | `.notCloned` | on GitHub, no clone under the root | `clone(nameWithOwner:into:)` | | `.notRegistered` | clone on disk, unknown to the store | `register(path:)` | | `.missing` | registered path no longer on disk | `forget(repoID:)` | | `.misplaced(expected:)` | under a configured owner, wrong owner or visibility folder | `move(from:to:)` | | `.outOfScope(.fork/.archived/.otherRoot)` | listed with its reason, never acted on | — | ### The invariant that carries the weight `RepoTreeLayout.slot(forPath:)` returns `nil` — not a guess — for any path that is not exactly `///` with `owner` among the configured owners. That `nil` is what keeps `_worktrees/`, `_local-only/` and `customers/` out of every sweep that follows, and it is why the layout is a value type in `ElliotModel` rather than a few string operations inside the scanner. The second load-bearing rule: **the disk is the authority on presence.** A `RepoSlot` exists only where the scanner saw a `.git`, so a registered path with no slot is `.missing` — a different row, and a different fix, from one that was never cloned. ### Persistence A `v2_repositoryLayout` migration, additive — GRDB's migrator appends to `v1_initial`: `setting(key TEXT PRIMARY KEY, value TEXT NOT NULL)` holding the JSON-encoded `RepoTreeLayout`, and a nullable `repo.visibility TEXT` so the expected path is recomputable without a network call. The pre-existing `migrations()` and `repoRoundTrip()` tests passing unchanged is what proves a `v1` database survives. ### Testing `RepoTreeLayoutTests` and `RepoReconcilerTests` are pure — no filesystem, no network — and the reconciler is tested against a fixture shaped like the real tree: two owners, both visibilities, a fork, an archived repository, a clone under `_worktrees/`, a clone under the wrong visibility. `RepoTreeScannerTests` uses real directories in `FileManager.default.temporaryDirectory`. `GHRepoSummaryTests` decodes a captured `gh repo list --json` payload committed under `Fixtures/gh/`, alongside the existing `Fixtures/stream-json/` — the decoder's contract is `gh`'s field names, and those are checked against a real payload rather than a hand-written guess.
## 🛠️ Implementation plan > **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking. **Goal:** Compute, for every repository of the configured GitHub owners, exactly one verdict describing how GitHub, the disk and the store disagree — plus the persistence and the two read-only sources it needs. **Architecture:** The verdict is a pure function of three lists (GitHub, disk, store) computed in `ElliotModel`; the two read-only sources — `gh repo list` and a shallow tree scan — live in `ElliotProcess` and `ElliotEngine`. Nothing here writes to disk or touches `ElliotApp`. Tasks run in strict target-dependency order. **Tech Stack:** Swift 6.1 language mode, macOS 15+, Swift Testing (`@Suite` / `@Test` / `#expect`), GRDB 7, `gh` and `git` driven through the existing `ProcessRunner`. ### Global Constraints - Swift tools version **6.1**, `swiftLanguageModes: [.v6]`, platform **macOS 15** — do not raise any of them (`ElliotKit/Package.swift:1-5,51`). - **`ElliotModel` stays dependency-free.** No GRDB, no `MCP`. Persistence conformance goes in `ElliotStore/Records.swift`, never in a model file. - **`ElliotMCPKit` must not gain a dependency** on `ElliotEngine` or `ElliotProcess` (`Package.swift:35-41`). This issue adds no MCP tool. - **No `git` write verb at all in this issue.** No `clone`, `relocate`, `pull`, `fetch`, `merge`, `rebase`, `stash`, `push`, `commit`, `checkout`, and no deletion of a working tree — in code or in a test. `RepoFix` declares the cases; the follow-up applies them. - Tests use **Swift Testing**: `@Suite("") struct Tests`, matching `ElliotKit/Tests/`. - Build and test with `cd ElliotKit && swift test`; one suite with `swift test --filter `. - Commit identity: `Philippe Matray `. Conventional commits scoped by target — `feat(model):`, `feat(store):`, `feat(process):`, `feat(engine):`. - Every temporary directory a test creates lives under `FileManager.default.temporaryDirectory` and is removed in the test. **No test may write anywhere under `~/Repositories`.** --- ### Task 1: `RepoTreeLayout` — the path ⇄ slot mapping **Files:** create `ElliotKit/Sources/ElliotModel/RepoTreeLayout.swift`; test `ElliotKit/Tests/ElliotModelTests/RepoTreeLayoutTests.swift`. **Interfaces:** produces `RepoVisibility` (`.public`/`.private`, `init(ghVisibility:)`, `CaseIterable`), `RepoSlot(owner:visibility:name:)` with `nameWithOwner`, and `RepoTreeLayout(root:owners:)` with `expectedPath(nameWithOwner:visibility:)`, `slot(forPath:)`, `ownerDirectories()`, `static var portfolio`. Every later task consumes these. - [x] **Step 1: Write the failing test** ```swift import Foundation import Testing @testable import ElliotModel @Suite("Repo tree layout") struct RepoTreeLayoutTests { let layout = RepoTreeLayout(root: "/Users/p/Repositories", owners: ["phmatray", "Atypical-Consulting"]) @Test("An expected path is owner, then visibility, then bare name") func expectedPath() { #expect(layout.expectedPath(nameWithOwner: "phmatray/Koine", visibility: .private) == "/Users/p/Repositories/phmatray/private/Koine") #expect(layout.expectedPath(nameWithOwner: "Atypical-Consulting/og-engine", visibility: .public) == "/Users/p/Repositories/Atypical-Consulting/public/og-engine") } @Test("An unconfigured owner, or a name without one, has no expected path") func unknownOwner() { #expect(layout.expectedPath(nameWithOwner: "torvalds/linux", visibility: .public) == nil) #expect(layout.expectedPath(nameWithOwner: "no-slash", visibility: .public) == nil) } @Test("A path parses back into its slot") func slotRoundTrip() { #expect(layout.slot(forPath: "/Users/p/Repositories/phmatray/private/Koine") == RepoSlot(owner: "phmatray", visibility: .private, name: "Koine")) } @Test("Everything outside owner/visibility/name is out of scope, not misplaced") func outOfScope() { for path in [ "/Users/p/Repositories/_worktrees/Elliot", "/Users/p/Repositories/_local-only/Yendor", "/Users/p/Repositories/customers/netimpex/api", "/Users/p/Repositories/repo-audit", "/Users/p/Repositories/phmatray/Koine", // no visibility folder "/Users/p/Repositories/phmatray/archived/Koine", // not a visibility folder "/Users/p/Repositories/phmatray/private/Koine/nested", // too deep "/elsewhere/phmatray/private/Koine", // outside the root ] { #expect(layout.slot(forPath: path) == nil, "\(path) must not parse") } } @Test("A trailing slash on the root does not change the answer") func rootNormalisation() { let slashed = RepoTreeLayout(root: "/Users/p/Repositories/", owners: ["phmatray"]) #expect(slashed.slot(forPath: "/Users/p/Repositories/phmatray/public/lenia") == RepoSlot(owner: "phmatray", visibility: .public, name: "lenia")) } @Test("gh's INTERNAL visibility is filed as private") func internalIsPrivate() { #expect(RepoVisibility(ghVisibility: "PUBLIC") == .public) #expect(RepoVisibility(ghVisibility: "INTERNAL") == .private) #expect(RepoVisibility(ghVisibility: "PRIVATE") == .private) } } ``` - [x] **Step 2: Run it and watch it fail** Run: `cd ElliotKit && swift test --filter RepoTreeLayoutTests` → FAIL, `cannot find 'RepoTreeLayout' in scope`. - [x] **Step 3: Write `RepoTreeLayout.swift`** ```swift import Foundation /// Where a repository belongs on disk. /// /// The portfolio is laid out `///`. Anything /// that does not match that exactly — a sibling root like `_worktrees/`, a /// nested directory, an owner we do not manage — is **out of scope**, not /// misplaced: `slot(forPath:)` answers `nil` rather than guessing, because the /// caller's next move would be to offer to move the directory. public struct RepoTreeLayout: Codable, Sendable, Hashable { public var root: String public var owners: [String] public init(root: String, owners: [String]) { self.root = Self.normalise(root) self.owners = owners } /// The default this machine is laid out for. public static var portfolio: RepoTreeLayout { RepoTreeLayout(root: NSHomeDirectory() + "/Repositories", owners: ["phmatray", "Atypical-Consulting"]) } public func ownerDirectories() -> [String] { owners.flatMap { owner in RepoVisibility.allCases.map { "\(root)/\(owner)/\($0.rawValue)" } } } public func expectedPath(nameWithOwner: String, visibility: RepoVisibility) -> String? { let parts = nameWithOwner.split(separator: "/", omittingEmptySubsequences: false) guard parts.count == 2, !parts[1].isEmpty, owners.contains(String(parts[0])) else { return nil } return "\(root)/\(parts[0])/\(visibility.rawValue)/\(parts[1])" } public func slot(forPath path: String) -> RepoSlot? ## What happened Leaving edit mode in the card detail sheet kills the app. `EXC_BREAKPOINT (SIGTRAP)` on the main thread, trapping inside SwiftUI: ``` 0 SwiftUICore BindingOperations.ForceUnwrapping.get(base:) + 304 1 SwiftUICore protocol witness for Projection.get(base:) in conformance BindingOperations.ForceUnwrapping 2 SwiftUICore ProjectedLocation.update() … 8 SwiftUICore _DynamicPropertyBuffer.update(container:phase:) 13 SwiftUICore DynamicBody.updateValue() … 25 SwiftUI NSHostingView.layout() ``` `esr: 0xf2000001 (Breakpoint) brk 1` — a force-unwrap of `nil`, not a memory fault. The crashing type is named outright in the register state: `x2`/`x14`/`x19`/`x22` hold **`type metadata for CardDraft`** and `x9` points at **`getEnumTagSinglePayload for CardDraft`** — SwiftUI reading the optional's enum tag, finding `.none`, and trapping. **The single culprit is `ElliotKit/Sources/ElliotApp/CardView.swift:133`:** ```swift @State private var draft: CardDraft? // line 124 … if let editable = Binding($draft) { // line 133 CardFieldsEditor(draft: editable) // line 135 } ``` `Binding.init?(_ base: Binding)` hands back a binding backed by `BindingOperations.ForceUnwrapping` — a projection that force-unwraps **on every read**, not just at the point of construction. `CardFieldsEditor` stores that projection in its `_DynamicPropertyBuffer`. The moment `draft` goes back to `nil` the child is still mounted, SwiftUI refreshes its dynamic properties before tearing it down, `ForceUnwrapping.get(base:)` reads `.none`, and it traps. There are exactly two places that write `nil`, and **both are user-reachable in one click**: | Line | Action | Note | |---|---|---| | `CardView.swift:150` | **Cancel** — `self.draft = nil` | synchronous | | `CardView.swift:211` | **Save** succeeds — `self.draft = nil` | inside a `Task`, so it lands on a *later* runloop turn — the child is fully mounted and guaranteed an update pass | This is the only `Binding($optional)` in the codebase (`grep -rn 'Binding(\$' ElliotKit/Sources/` → one hit), so the blast radius is this one sheet. `BoardView.swift:30`'s `.sheet(item: $model.pendingFollowUps)` is a different, safe construct — `.sheet(item:)` hands the closure a *value* and lets SwiftUI own the lifetime. Introduced by `f78a395` — *"feat(app): correct a card's label and story until it is filed (#5) (#6)"* — merged today. Edit mode is new, so both `nil` transitions are new. ## Steps to reproduce 1. Launch `dist/Elliot.app` with a registered repo holding at least one **Backlog** card that has **no issue number** (the Edit button is gated on `card.issueNumber == nil`). 2. Open that card's detail sheet. 3. Click **Edit** — the field editor appears (`draft` becomes non-`nil`, the projection is created and handed to `CardFieldsEditor`). 4. Click **Cancel**. *Or*: change the label and click **Save**, and let the save succeed. 5. 💥 The app terminates with `EXC_BREAKPOINT` in `BindingOperations.ForceUnwrapping.get(base:)`. Observed on macOS 26.5.2 (25F84), Elliot 0.1.0 (1), arm64, SwiftUI/SwiftUICore 7.5.3. Crash report `4A2A0DB5-DBFC-4FED-9C26-6346CD918BE2`, 20 s after launch. (A `ProcessRunner.run` was mid-flight on thread 1 — incidental, not causal; that thread is parked in `waitUntilExit`.) ## Expected Cancel returns the sheet to its read-only view with the card unchanged. Save writes the edit, returns to read-only, and shows the new label. Neither ends the process. ## Area `ElliotApp` (the detail sheet), plus `ElliotModel` for the extracted, testable edit state. **Related:** #5, #6, #8 > #8 — *"Run the manual GUI verification owed by #5/#6 (card edit sheet)"* — is the verification that > would have caught this. This issue is the concrete defect; #8 remains the standing manual check.
🧠 Brainstorm ### Problem / context The detail sheet models edit mode as `Optional`: `nil` means read-only, non-`nil` means editing. That is a tidy way to say it, but it forces the view to derive a *non-optional* binding for `CardFieldsEditor` (whose contract is `@Binding var draft: CardDraft`, shared with `NewCardSheet`). `Binding($draft)` is the standard way to do that derivation — and it is a trap that fires whenever the optional empties while the child is alive. It is not a race, not a rare timing window: it is every Cancel and every successful Save. The fix has a constraint the comment on lines 129–132 states explicitly: > `Binding($draft)` rather than a hand-rolled get/set: a getter that closed over the unwrapped local > would keep reporting the value as it was when the body was last evaluated, so two mutations in one > action would lose the first. That is a real bug they already hit — `CardDraft.removeCriterion(at:)` carries a doc comment about exactly the same staleness, which is why it re-seeds the empty row in *one* mutation. So a fix must keep the binding **reading through live state**, not through a captured local. Reverting to a closure over an unwrapped local trades a crash for a data-loss bug. Two further constraints from the repo's own grain: - `ElliotApp` is an `.executableTarget` with **no test target**. `CardDraft`'s doc comment says the quiet part: *"a validation rule written in a `View` is a validation rule nothing can check."* A fix that lives entirely in `CardView.swift` cannot be regression-tested. - Swift 6 language mode, strict concurrency — anything new must be `Sendable`. ### Approaches **A — non-optional draft + an explicit `isEditing` flag, lifted into a testable `ElliotModel` type.** Replace `@State private var draft: CardDraft?` with `@State private var editor = CardEditor()`, where `CardEditor` holds a **non-optional** `draft` and a `Bool`. The child then binds to `$editor.draft` — a plain key-path scope on non-optional state. No projection, no optional, nothing to unwrap, so `BindingOperations.ForceUnwrapping` never enters the graph. Leaving edit mode flips a `Bool` and *keeps* the draft value, so nothing is destroyed underneath a mounted child. *For:* deletes the crashing construct instead of defending against it; `$editor.draft` reads through `@State` so it is exactly as live as `Binding($draft)` was — the 129–132 concern is fully honoured; putting the transitions in `ElliotModel` makes them unit-testable, which the current shape is not. *Against:* two facts (`isEditing`, `draft`) where there was one, so they could in principle drift — mitigated by `private(set) var isEditing` and by the transitions being methods on the type rather than assignments scattered through the view. **B — a defaulting binding: `Binding(get: { draft ?? CardDraft(card: card) }, set: { draft = $0 })`.** Reads `self.draft` through the `@State` wrapper rather than a captured local, so it stays live, and a `nil` read yields the fallback instead of trapping. *For:* smallest possible diff; keeps `Optional` as the state shape. *Against:* keeps a projection in the graph whose safety rests entirely on a fallback nobody will remember is load-bearing. It converts a loud crash into a silent one-frame flash of a resurrected draft during teardown, and re-seeds `CardDraft(card: card)` on every read while editing. Defensive, not correct. **C — present the editor through `.sheet(item:)`.** `.sheet(item:)` takes `Binding` and hands the closure a *value*, so SwiftUI owns the lifetime and the `nil` transition is a dismissal rather than a mid-layout unwrap. *For:* uses the framework's own answer to "optional drives presentation"; matches `BoardView.swift:30`. *Against:* `CardFieldsEditor` needs a two-way binding and `item:` gives a value, so it needs a nested `@State` copy plus write-back on save — more machinery than the bug warrants. It also changes the UX (a sheet stacked on a sheet) for what is meant to be inline edit mode. ### Recommendation **A.** It removes the construct rather than guarding it, it is the only option that leaves an automated regression test behind (B and C are both view-shaped and therefore untestable in this repo), and it satisfies the staleness constraint the original comment was written to protect. B's correctness depends on a fallback that reads like dead code; C rebuilds the presentation for a bug that is really about the shape of the state. **Assumptions** *(defaulted, not asked)*: (1) the `Edit` button stays gated on `card.issueNumber == nil` — the "once filed, the issue is the record" rule is unchanged, and the fix moves that gate into the tested type rather than dropping it; (2) `CardFieldsEditor`'s public shape (`@Binding var draft: CardDraft`) stays as-is, since `NewCardSheet` shares it; (3) the `ForEach(draft.criteria.indices, id: \.self)` remove-row pattern in `CardFieldsEditor:57-71` is **out of scope** — it is a genuine hazard of the same family, but it is already defended by the `indices.contains` guards and by `removeCriterion(at:)`'s own bounds check, and it is not what this crash report shows.
📋 Spec ### Goal Leaving edit mode — by Cancel or by a successful Save — never traps. Prove it with a unit test that does not require launching the app. ### Non-goals - Reworking `CardFieldsEditor` or `NewCardSheet`; their contract is unchanged. - Adding an `ElliotAppTests` target. `ElliotApp` stays untested by design; the fix is to move the state out of it, matching what `CardDraft` already does. - The criteria-row `ForEach(indices, id: \.self)` pattern (already guarded — see Assumptions). - Changing the "once filed, edit on GitHub" rule. ### The crashing path today ```mermaid flowchart TD A["@State draft: CardDraft? — line 124"] B["Binding of CardDraft, backed by
BindingOperations.ForceUnwrapping — line 133"] C["CardFieldsEditor holds it in
_DynamicPropertyBuffer — line 135"] D["Cancel line 150, or Save success line 211
sets draft = nil"] E["next layout pass:
ProjectedLocation.update calls get"] F{"base is .none?"} G["EXC_BREAKPOINT — brk 1"] H["value delivered"] A -->|"Binding of the projected value"| B B --> C C --> E D --> A A -.->|"now .none"| E E --> F F -->|"yes — today"| G F -->|"no"| H ``` The fix removes node **B** entirely, so **F** never has a `.none` to answer for. ### New public surface — `ElliotModel/CardEditor.swift` ```swift /// Edit mode for the card detail sheet: whether it is editing, and the draft /// it is editing. /// /// Two fields rather than an `Optional`, because the sheet binds a /// child editor to the draft. A binding derived from an optional with /// `Binding($draft)` is backed by `BindingOperations.ForceUnwrapping`, which /// traps the moment the optional empties while the child is still mounted — /// every Cancel, every successful Save. Keeping the draft non-optional means /// there is no projection to trap, and `end()` destroys nothing underneath a /// view that is still on screen. public struct CardEditor: Sendable, Hashable { public private(set) var isEditing: Bool public var draft: CardDraft public init() /// Enters edit mode seeded from the card. Refuses once the card is filed: /// from that point the issue is the record, not the card. public mutating func begin(from card: Card) /// Leaves edit mode. The draft is deliberately kept — nothing reads it /// while `isEditing` is false. public mutating func end() } ``` ### Behaviour | Call | `isEditing` | `draft` | |---|---|---| | `init()` | `false` | `CardDraft()` | | `begin(from:)`, `card.issueNumber == nil` | `true` | `CardDraft(card: card)` | | `begin(from:)`, `card.issueNumber != nil` | unchanged (`false`) | **unchanged** — a filed card must not clobber a draft | | `end()` | `false` | **unchanged** — this is the property that fixes the crash | ### Call-site changes — `ElliotApp/CardView.swift` | Now | After | |---|---| | `@State private var draft: CardDraft?` (124) | `@State private var editor = CardEditor()` | | `if let editable = Binding($draft)` (133) | `if editor.isEditing` | | `CardFieldsEditor(draft: editable)` (135) | `CardFieldsEditor(draft: $editor.draft)` | | `if draft == nil, card.issueNumber == nil` (145) | `if !editor.isEditing, card.issueNumber == nil` | | `draft = CardDraft(card: card)` (146) | `editor.begin(from: card)` | | `if let draft` (149) | `if editor.isEditing` | | `self.draft = nil` (150, Cancel) | `editor.end()` | | `save(draft)` / `!draft.isValid` (151–153) | `save(editor.draft)` / `!editor.draft.isValid` | | `self.draft = nil` (211, Save ✓) | `editor.end()` | The 129–132 comment is replaced by one that records *why* the state is not an optional, so the next reader does not "simplify" it back into a crash. ### Edge cases - **Save fails** (card filed or deleted mid-edit): `updateCard` returns `false`, `editor.end()` is **not** called, `saveError` is shown, and the typed text survives — unchanged from today. - **Card filed while the sheet is open:** `begin(from:)` refuses, and the Edit button is already hidden by the `card.issueNumber == nil` check that stays in the view. Two guards, deliberately — one testable, one visible. - **Cancel then Edit again:** `begin(from:)` re-seeds from the card, so a cancelled draft is never resurrected even though the value was retained. - **Draft retained after `end()`:** intentional, and the crux of the fix — nothing reads `draft` while `isEditing` is `false`, and retaining it is what keeps a live child binding valid through the teardown pass. ### Verification `CardEditorTests` (a new `@Suite` in `ElliotModelTests`) covers the transition table above — including the one that reproduces the bug: **`end()` must leave `draft` intact**, which is what makes the child's binding safe through teardown. Because the fix is ultimately view-shaped, the suite proves the state machine, not the SwiftUI graph; the on-screen confirmation is the manual step in Task 3 and belongs to the standing check in #8.
## 🛠️ Implementation plan > **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking. **Goal:** remove `BindingOperations.ForceUnwrapping` from the card detail sheet's view graph, so Cancel and Save cannot trap. **Architecture:** Swift Package Manager, package root `ElliotKit/`. Layer order — `ElliotModel` (no dependencies) → `ElliotStore`/`ElliotProcess`/`ElliotIPC` → `ElliotEngine` → `ElliotMCPKit`/`ElliotApp`. This change touches `ElliotModel` first, then `ElliotApp`. **Tech stack:** Swift 6.1 toolchain, `swiftLanguageModes: [.v6]`, `.macOS(.v15)`, swift-testing (`@Suite`/`@Test`/`#expect`), SwiftUI. **Global constraints:** - Run every `swift` command from `ElliotKit/` — there is no manifest at the repo root. - Strict concurrency: `CardEditor` must be `Sendable` (it is, structurally — all members are). - `ElliotApp` has **no test target**. Do not add one; put the logic in `ElliotModel` so it can be tested, exactly as `CardDraft` already is. - Do not change `CardFieldsEditor`'s `@Binding var draft: CardDraft` — `NewCardSheet` shares it. - Keep the "once filed, the issue is the record" rule: a card with an `issueNumber` is not editable. - Commit identity: `git -c user.email=phmatray@gmail.com -c user.name="Philippe Matray"`. - Conventional Commits, module scope, title ends in `(#)`. - No formatter is configured in this repo — match the surrounding style by hand (4-space indent, doc comments that explain *why*). ### Task 1: `CardEditor` — the edit-mode state, in a target that has tests **Files:** create `ElliotKit/Sources/ElliotModel/CardEditor.swift`; create test `ElliotKit/Tests/ElliotModelTests/CardEditorTests.swift`. **Interfaces:** `public struct CardEditor: Sendable, Hashable` with `public private(set) var isEditing: Bool`, `public var draft: CardDraft`, `public init()`, `public mutating func begin(from card: Card)`, `public mutating func end()`. Semantics are the transition table in the spec. - [x] **Step 1:** Write the failing suite in `CardEditorTests.swift` — `@Suite("Card editor")`, matching the style of `CardDraftTests`. Cover: a fresh editor is not editing; `begin(from:)` on an unfiled card sets `isEditing` and seeds the draft from the card (title and story fields); `begin(from:)` on a card with an `issueNumber` is refused and leaves both fields untouched; **`end()` clears `isEditing` but leaves `draft` intact** (the regression case — name it so, and say in the test why); `begin` → `end` → `begin` re-seeds from the card rather than resurrecting the cancelled draft. - [x] **Step 2:** Run `cd ElliotKit && swift test --filter CardEditorTests` → FAIL (`cannot find 'CardEditor' in scope`). - [x] **Step 3:** Implement `CardEditor.swift` per the spec's public surface. Carry the doc comment that records *why* the draft is not an `Optional` — cite `BindingOperations.ForceUnwrapping` by name so the next reader does not "simplify" it back. - [x] **Step 4:** Run `cd ElliotKit && swift test --filter CardEditorTests` → PASS. - [x] **Step 5:** Commit: `feat(model): CardEditor holds edit mode without an optional draft` ### Task 2: Rewire `CardDetailView` onto `CardEditor` **Files:** modify `ElliotKit/Sources/ElliotApp/CardView.swift` (lines 124–162 and `save(_:)` at 208–219). **Interfaces:** no public API change. `@State private var editor = CardEditor()` replaces `@State private var draft: CardDraft?`; `CardFieldsEditor(draft: $editor.draft)` replaces the `Binding($draft)` projection. Apply the call-site table from the spec in full. - [x] **Step 1:** Replace `@State private var draft: CardDraft?` (line 124) with `@State private var editor = CardEditor()`. - [x] **Step 2:** Replace the `if let editable = Binding($draft)` branch (133–141) with `if editor.isEditing`, passing `$editor.draft` to `CardFieldsEditor`. Replace the 129–132 comment with one explaining why the state is not an optional (the projection traps on teardown) rather than why a closure was avoided. - [x] **Step 3:** Rewire the button row (145–156): `!editor.isEditing` for the Edit gate, `editor.begin(from: card)` for Edit, `editor.end()` for Cancel, `editor.draft` for Save and the `isValid` check. Keep the `card.issueNumber == nil` gate on the Edit button. - [x] **Step 4:** In `save(_:)` (208–219) replace `self.draft = nil` with `editor.end()` on the success branch only — the failure branch must still stay in edit mode with the typed text. - [x] **Step 5:** Verify no `Binding($` remains: `grep -rn 'Binding(\$' ElliotKit/Sources/` → **no output**. - [x] **Step 6:** Run `cd ElliotKit && swift build` → builds clean, no new warnings. - [x] **Step 7:** Run the full suite `cd ElliotKit && swift test` → PASS (re-run once if the fake-claude suites flake; see #7). - [x] **Step 8:** Commit: `fix(app): card edit sheet no longer traps on Cancel or Save` ### Task 3: Confirm on screen, and record it **Files:** modify `README.md` only if the *Status* section's "not done" list needs amending. - [x] **Step 1:** Build the bundle: `./Scripts/build-app.sh && open dist/Elliot.app`. - [x] **Step 2:** Walk the reproduction from *Steps to reproduce* on an unfiled Backlog card: Edit → **Cancel**. The sheet returns to read-only, the new label shows on the board, the app survives. - [x] **Step 4:** Exercise the criteria rows while in edit mode (add two, remove the middle one, remove the last one) — confirm no trap, since `ForEach(indices, id: \.self)` is the same family of hazard and this is the cheapest moment to check it. - [x] **Step 5:** Confirm a **filed** card (one with an issue number) still shows no Edit button and the "edit it on GitHub" note. - [x] **Step 6:** Post the outcome as a comment on this issue and on #8, naming the macOS and app version tested. - [x] **Step 7:** Commit any README amendment: `docs: record the card-edit crash fix in Status` (skip this step if the README needed no change). — *Skipped: the Status section's "Not done" list describes gaps, not bugs, and never mentioned this crash, so it needed no change.*
title: Card edit sheet crashes on Cancel and on Save: Binding($draft) force-unwraps a nil CardDraft

body:
## User story **As a** developer, **I want** to correct a card's label, story and acceptance criteria from its detail sheet, **so that** a typo in a story does not force me to delete the card and type the whole thing again. ## Acceptance criteria 1. The card detail sheet offers **Edit** for a card that has not been filed yet (`issueNumber == nil`). 2. Saving goes through `BoardService.updateCard` — the method that exists at `ElliotKit/Sources/ElliotEngine/BoardService.swift:174` and that **nothing calls today**. 3. A card that already carries an issue number is **not** editable here, and the sheet says why — the issue is the record from that point on. ## Problem `CardDetailView` (`ElliotKit/Sources/ElliotApp/CardView.swift:119`) is read-only. It renders the title, the story or the note, the runs, and a **Done** button. There is no way back into the fields. So a card written with a typo has exactly one repair path: context-menu → **Delete card** → **New backlog item** → retype the label, the three story parts and every acceptance criterion. `NewCardSheet` (`ElliotKit/Sources/ElliotApp/Sheets.swift:8`) is the only place those fields have ever been editable, and it only ever creates. The write path is already built and already unused. `BoardService.updateCard(_:)` is a two-line passthrough to `store.saveCard`, and `grep -rn updateCard --include="*.swift" .` returns exactly one hit — its own definition. The board can already store an edit; nothing asks it to. ## Proposed solution Make `CardDetailView` a two-mode sheet — read-only by default, editable on demand — and give it the same field set `NewCardSheet` already uses, extracted so the two share one editor rather than two copies of the same validation. Gate the edit on `issueNumber == nil`, in two places for two different reasons: the sheet hides the button (so a filed card never *offers* the wrong thing) and `BoardService.updateCard` refuses the write (so the rule is testable, which the SwiftUI layer is not — `ElliotApp` is an `executableTarget` with no test target). ## Area `app` (`ElliotKit/Sources/ElliotApp/`) with a supporting change in `engine` (`ElliotEngine`) and a new value type in `model` (`ElliotModel`).
🧠 Brainstorm ### Problem / context The backlog holds **user stories**, not free text — `UserStory` (`ElliotKit/Sources/ElliotModel/UserStory.swift`) keeps `role` / `want` / `benefit` / `acceptanceCriteria` as four separate fields, deliberately: *"they can be validated, rendered consistently into an issue, and — the reason this is structured at all — generated from a repository later without having to parse prose back apart."* That structure is exactly what makes a typo expensive. The story is not one text field you re-edit; it is four, plus a board label, plus a story-vs-note mode. Losing them all to fix one word is the whole complaint. Two facts about the codebase shape every option below: - **`BoardService.updateCard` already exists and has zero callers.** This issue is not "add a write path", it is "wire the one that is already there" — and, while wiring it, decide what it should refuse. - **`ElliotApp` is an `executableTarget`** (`ElliotKit/Package.swift:23`) with no `ElliotAppTests`. Any rule that lives only in a SwiftUI `View` cannot be tested by `swift test`. Rules have to move down a layer to be provable. Prior art in the repo: `NewCardSheet` already implements the entire field set — segmented story/note picker, the three story fields, an add/remove list of acceptance criteria, a live "What create-issue will receive" preview, and a `canAdd` guard that refuses a half-written story *before* the first drag would refuse it. None of that should be written twice. ### Approaches **A. Extract the fields into a shared editor; `CardDetailView` toggles read-only ⇄ edit.** *(recommended)* Pull `NewCardSheet`'s field block into a `CardFieldsEditor` view backed by a `CardDraft` value type in `ElliotModel`. `NewCardSheet` keeps its behaviour by binding to a fresh draft; `CardDetailView` binds to a draft seeded from the card. - ✅ One field set, one validation rule, one preview — a fix lands in both sheets at once. - ✅ `CardDraft` lives in `ElliotModel` (dependency-free, per the target order), so *"is this saveable?"* becomes a unit test instead of something only a human clicking the app can check. - ✅ Save/Cancel is an explicit boundary: nothing reaches the store until the draft validates. - ⚠️ Touches `NewCardSheet`, which currently works. Mitigated by the draft being a pure value type with its own tests, and by `NewCardSheet`'s behaviour being unchanged by construction (same predicate, same derivation). **B. A separate `EditCardSheet`.** Copy `NewCardSheet`, prefill `@State` from the card, swap **Add** for **Save**. - ✅ Smallest diff to existing code; `NewCardSheet` is untouched. - ❌ Duplicates ~60 lines of fields plus `canAdd`, `previewStory` and the criteria add/remove logic. Two places to fix the next validation bug, and they will drift — the preview box is the obvious first casualty. - ❌ Leaves the validation rule in the untestable target. **C. Inline per-field editing in the detail sheet.** Tap a field, it becomes a `TextField`, it writes on blur. - ✅ Feels direct; no mode switch. - ❌ No atomic validation boundary — a story mid-edit is incomplete by definition, so either the store accepts half-written stories or every keystroke is refused. - ❌ The story ⇄ note choice has no natural home: it is a property of the card, not of a field. - ❌ Each blur is a `saveCard`, so `updatedAt` churns on cards nobody meaningfully changed. ### Recommendation **A.** The duplication argument alone decides it against B, and B's copy would land the validation in the one target `swift test` cannot reach — the repo's own structural argument for `UserStory` ("kept as separate fields … because they can be validated") applies just as much to the draft that produces one. C trades away the save boundary that makes the `issueNumber` guard expressible at all. ### The second decision: what `updateCard` should refuse Wiring the first caller is the moment to look at the signature. `updateCard(_ card: Card)` takes a whole `Card` and writes it verbatim — which means it will happily persist a changed `column`. The repo's stated invariant is *"`BoardService` is the only thing that changes a card's column … Never add a second path that mutates a column."* A whole-`Card` write **is** that second path; it has only never fired because nothing calls it. So the recommendation narrows the method to the three user-authored fields and adds the filed-card refusal: ```swift public func updateCard(id: UUID, title: String, body: String, story: UserStory?) async throws ``` A card's column, order, issue, PR and branch become unreachable through this door — they keep their one real owner — and `BoardError` gains `cardAlreadyFiled(Int)` so acceptance criterion 3 is a test, not a hidden button.
📋 Spec ### Goal A card that has not been filed can have its board label, its story (role / want / benefit / acceptance criteria) or its plain note corrected from the card detail sheet, without deleting and re-creating it. ### Scope - `CardDraft` — a new value type in `ElliotModel` holding the editable shape of a card and the rule for when it may be saved. - `BoardService.updateCard` — narrowed to the editable fields, refusing a filed card. - `CardFieldsEditor` — the field block extracted from `NewCardSheet`, bound to a `CardDraft`. - `CardDetailView` — read-only ⇄ edit toggle, plus the explanation for a filed card. - `AppModel.updateCard` — the view's route to the board, alongside `createCard` / `deleteCard`. ### Non-goals - Editing a **filed** card (`issueNumber != nil`) anywhere in the app. GitHub is the editor from that point on — this issue closes the door and explains it, it does not open a different one. - Editing `column`, `orderIndex`, `issueNumber`, `prNumber` or `branch`. Those belong to the move funnel and the watchers. - Re-syncing an already-filed issue's body from the card. Different feature, opposite direction. - Undo / edit history. `updatedAt` is stamped by `BoardStore.saveCard`; that is the whole audit trail this issue adds. ### State ```mermaid stateDiagram-v2 [*] --> ReadOnly: sheet opens ReadOnly --> Editing: Edit (issueNumber == nil) Editing --> ReadOnly: Cancel (draft discarded) Editing --> Saving: Save (draft.isValid) Saving --> ReadOnly: BoardService.updateCard succeeded Saving --> Editing: cardAlreadyFiled / cardNotFound ReadOnly --> Locked: issueNumber != nil Locked --> [*]: "Filed as #N — edit it on GitHub" ReadOnly --> [*]: Done ``` ### Write path ```mermaid flowchart LR A[CardDetailView
Save] --> B[AppModel.updateCard] B --> C[BoardService.updateCard
